# CELL 1: IMPORTS AND SPARK SESSION
# ---------------------------------
# This cell sets up the tools we need and ensures we have a Spark session.

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql import functions as F       # Common SQL-style functions (avg, count, etc.)
from pyspark.sql.window import Window        # For "per-group" ordering and row numbering

# Machine Learning tools from PySpark
from pyspark.ml import Pipeline
from pyspark.ml.feature import StringIndexer, OneHotEncoder, VectorAssembler

# Classification models we will use (4 different pipelines)
from pyspark.ml.classification import (
    LogisticRegression,          # Pipeline 1: baseline linear classifier
    RandomForestClassifier,      # Pipeline 2: tree ensemble
    GBTClassifier,               # Pipeline 3: gradient boosted trees
    MultilayerPerceptronClassifier  # Pipeline 4: neural network
)

from pyspark.ml.evaluation import BinaryClassificationEvaluator  # For AUC, AUPR

# Create or get an existing Spark session.
# In Databricks, "spark" usually exists already, but this is safe to run.
spark = (
    SparkSession.builder
    .appName("MIMIC_IV_Gender_Bias_Mortality")
    .getOrCreate()
)

# CELL 3: LOAD MIMIC-IV TABLES
# ----------------------------
# This helper function loads one compressed CSV file into a Spark DataFrame.
# We assume the first row contains column names (header=True), and we ask
# Spark to guess the data types (inferSchema=True).

def load_csv_gz(name: str):
    path = f"{DATA_BASE_PATH}/{files[name]}"
    print(f"Loading {name} from {path}")
    return spark.read.csv(path, header=True, inferSchema=True)

# Load each table we will use in this project.
admissions       = load_csv_gz("admissions")
patients         = load_csv_gz("patients")
diagnoses_icd    = load_csv_gz("diagnoses_icd")
procedures_icd   = load_csv_gz("procedures_icd")
drgcodes_df      = load_csv_gz("drgcodes")
services_df      = load_csv_gz("services")
transfers_df     = load_csv_gz("transfers")

print("Schemas for key tables:")
admissions.printSchema()
patients.printSchema()
diagnoses_icd.printSchema()
procedures_icd.printSchema()

# CELL 4: DEFINE COHORT AND JOIN ADMISSIONS + PATIENTS
# ----------------------------------------------------
# Goal:
#  - Keep ONLY adult patients (age >= 18).
#  - Join admissions with patients to attach gender and age to each admission.
#  - Compute hospital length of stay in days.

# 1) Filter to adult patients
patients_adult = (
    patients
    .filter(F.col("anchor_age") >= 18)
    .select(
        "subject_id",
        "gender",
        F.col("anchor_age").alias("age")
    )
)

# 2) Join admissions with adult patient demographics
adm_pt = (
    admissions.alias("a")
    .join(
        patients_adult.alias("p"),
        on="subject_id",
        how="inner"
    )
)

# 3) Compute hospital LOS
adm_pt = adm_pt.withColumn(
    "los_hosp_days",
    F.datediff(F.col("dischtime"), F.col("admittime")).cast("double")
)

# 4) Select final columns (use race instead of ethnicity)
adm_pt = adm_pt.select(
    "subject_id",
    "hadm_id",
    "gender",
    "age",
    F.col("race").alias("ethnicity"),   # <-- FIXED HERE
    "admission_type",
    "admission_location",
    "discharge_location",
    "insurance",
    "marital_status",
    "los_hosp_days",
    "hospital_expire_flag"
)

# CELL 5: CRUDE MORTALITY BY GENDER (REAL OUTCOMES)
# -------------------------------------------------
# Here we compute simple, unadjusted mortality rates by gender.
# This gives us an initial sense of whether male and female patients
# experience different in-hospital mortality rates.

mortality_by_gender = (
    adm_pt
    .groupBy("gender")
    .agg(
        F.count("*").alias("n_admissions"),
        F.avg(F.col("hospital_expire_flag").cast("double")).alias("mortality_rate")
        # hospital_expire_flag is 0 or 1 -> average = proportion of deaths
    )
)

print("Crude (unadjusted) mortality rate by gender:")
mortality_by_gender.show(truncate=False)

# CELL 6: FEATURE ENGINEERING - DIAGNOSES, PROCEDURES, DRG, SERVICE, TRANSFERS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# We create summary features per admission (hadm_id) that capture complexity:
#  - number of diagnoses
#  - number of procedures
#  - number of DRG codes
#  - first hospital service
#  - number of transfers (unit changes)

# 6.1 Diagnoses per admission
diag_agg = (
    diagnoses_icd
    .groupBy("hadm_id")
    .agg(
        F.count("*").alias("num_diagnoses"),
        F.countDistinct("icd_code").alias("num_unique_diagnoses")
    )
)

print("Diagnosis features per admission:")
diag_agg.show(5)

# 6.2 Procedures per admission
proc_agg = (
    procedures_icd
    .groupBy("hadm_id")
    .agg(
        F.count("*").alias("num_procedures"),
        F.countDistinct("icd_code").alias("num_unique_procedures")
    )
)

print("Procedure features per admission:")
proc_agg.show(5)

# 6.3 DRG codes per admission (severity proxy)
drg_agg = (
    drgcodes_df
    .groupBy("hadm_id")
    .agg(
        F.countDistinct("drg_code").alias("num_drg_codes")
    )
)

print("DRG features per admission:")
drg_agg.show(5)

# 6.4 First service per admission (e.g., MED, SURG)
w_service = Window.partitionBy("hadm_id").orderBy("transfertime")

service_first = (
    services_df
    .withColumn("rn", F.row_number().over(w_service))  # rank service records within each admission
    .filter(F.col("rn") == 1)                         # keep the first one
    .select("hadm_id", F.col("curr_service").alias("first_service"))
)

print("First service per admission:")
service_first.show(5)

# 6.5 Number of transfers per admission (instability proxy)
transfers_agg = (
    transfers_df
    .groupBy("hadm_id")
    .agg(F.count("*").alias("num_transfers"))
)

print("Number of transfers per admission:")
transfers_agg.show(5)

# CELL 7: FINAL ANALYTIC DATASET + CLEANING
# ----------------------------------------
# Now we join all these features together into one big table "df",
# where each row = one hospital admission.
# Then we perform a few basic cleaning steps.

# 7.1 Join everything onto the admissions + patients table
df = (
    adm_pt
    .join(diag_agg, on="hadm_id", how="left")
    .join(proc_agg, on="hadm_id", how="left")
    .join(drg_agg, on="hadm_id", how="left")
    .join(service_first, on="hadm_id", how="left")
    .join(transfers_agg, on="hadm_id", how="left")
)

# 7.2 Replace NULL counts with 0 (if no diagnoses/procedures/transfers, it means 0)
df = df.fillna({
    "num_diagnoses": 0,
    "num_unique_diagnoses": 0,
    "num_procedures": 0,
    "num_unique_procedures": 0,
    "num_drg_codes": 0,
    "num_transfers": 0
})

# 7.3 Basic cleaning rules:
# - Keep only rows with non-null gender and age
# - Remove strange or extreme LOS (negative or > 365 days)
# - Drop duplicate admissions if any

print("Row count BEFORE cleaning:", df.count())

df = df.filter(F.col("gender").isNotNull())
df = df.filter(F.col("age").isNotNull())
df = df.filter((F.col("los_hosp_days") >= 0) & (F.col("los_hosp_days") < 365))
df = df.dropDuplicates(["subject_id", "hadm_id"])

print("Row count AFTER cleaning:", df.count())

# 7.4 Create the ML label column for convenience.
# "label" = 1 if patient died in hospital, else 0.
df = df.withColumn("label", F.col("hospital_expire_flag").cast("double"))

print("Final analytic dataset sample:")
df.select(
    "subject_id", "hadm_id", "gender", "age", "ethnicity",
    "los_hosp_days", "num_diagnoses", "num_procedures",
    "num_transfers", "first_service", "label"
).show(10, truncate=False)

from pyspark.ml.evaluation import BinaryClassificationEvaluator
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, mean
from pyspark.ml.functions import vector_to_array

# AUC evaluator
evaluator_auc = BinaryClassificationEvaluator(
    labelCol="label",
    rawPredictionCol="rawPrediction",
    metricName="areaUnderROC"
)

# AUPR evaluator
evaluator_pr = BinaryClassificationEvaluator(
    labelCol="label",
    rawPredictionCol="rawPrediction",
    metricName="areaUnderPR"
)

print("Evaluators loaded successfully.")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# SAFE GENDER METRIC FUNCTION (NO RDDs)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
def compute_gender_metrics(pred_df, model_name):
    """
    Computes accuracy and avg predicted probability by gender.
    Works on serverless (no RDD operations).
    """

    print(f"\n=== Gender-specific metrics for {model_name} ===")

    # Extract probability for class 1
    pred_df = pred_df.withColumn(
        "prob1",
        vector_to_array("probability")[1]
    )

    # SAFE way to get gender list (NO RDDs)
    genders = [row["gender"] for row in pred_df.select("gender").distinct().collect()]

    for g in genders:
        subset = pred_df.filter(col("gender") == g)

        n = subset.count()
        if n == 0:
            continue

        accuracy = (
            subset.filter(col("prediction") == col("label")).count() / n
        )

        avg_prob = subset.select(mean("prob1")).collect()[0][0]

        print(f"Gender: {g} | n={n} | Accuracy={accuracy:.4f} | Avg Prob={avg_prob:.4f}")

    return True

print("Gender fairness metric function defined (serverless-safe).")

# CELL 9: ADVANCED FEATURE PREPROCESSING FOR ALL PIPELINES
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# This version supports:
#   - FeatureHasher (required for CE memory limits)
#   - PCA (for dimensionality reduction)
#   - Chi-Square feature selector (for categorical relevance)
#   - Feature importance selector (Random Forest–based)
#
# Each pipeline will choose which feature-selection method to use.

from pyspark.ml.feature import (
    FeatureHasher,
    PCA,
    ChiSqSelector
)

# --------------------------
# 1. Categorical input columns
# --------------------------
categorical_cols = [
    "gender",
    "ethnicity",
    "admission_type",
    "admission_location",
    "discharge_location",
    "insurance",
    "marital_status",
    "first_service"
]

# --------------------------
# 2. Numeric input columns
# --------------------------
numeric_cols = [
    "age",
    "los_hosp_days",
    "num_diagnoses",
    "num_unique_diagnoses",
    "num_procedures",
    "num_unique_procedures",
    "num_drg_codes",
    "num_transfers"
]

# --------------------------
# 3. Base FeatureHasher
# --------------------------
hasher = FeatureHasher(
    inputCols=categorical_cols + numeric_cols,
    outputCol="hashed_features",
    numFeatures=256
)

# --------------------------
# 4. PCA (for neural network pipeline)
# --------------------------
pca = PCA(
    k=64,                    # reduce 256 → 64 dims (safe for CE)
    inputCol="hashed_features",
    outputCol="pca_features"
)

# --------------------------
# 5. Chi-Square Selector (for GBT improvement)
# --------------------------
chi_selector = ChiSqSelector(
    numTopFeatures=128,
    featuresCol="hashed_features",
    labelCol="label",
    outputCol="chi_features"
)

# --------------------------
# 6. Placeholder for RF Feature Importance Selection
#    (computed dynamically in Pipeline 2)
# --------------------------
# We will populate this dynamically once RF is trained.

print("Advanced preprocessing components ready.")

# CELL 10 — SAFE GENDER FAIRNESS METRIC FUNCTION
# ----------------------------------------------

from pyspark.sql.functions import col, when, mean
from pyspark.ml.functions import vector_to_array

def compute_gender_metrics(df, model_name):
    """
    Computes fairness metrics by gender.
    df must already contain:
      - prediction column
      - label column
      - prob1 column (probability of class 1)
      - gender column
    """

    print(f"\n=== Gender-specific metrics for {model_name} ===")

    # Ensure prob1 exists (create it if missing)
    if "prob1" not in df.columns:
        df = df.withColumn("prob1", vector_to_array("probability")[1])

    genders = [row["gender"] for row in df.select("gender").distinct().collect()]

    metrics = []

    for g in genders:
        sub = df.filter(col("gender") == g)

        total = sub.count()
        if total == 0:
            continue

        accuracy = sub.filter(col("prediction") == col("label")).count() / total
        avg_prob = sub.select(mean("prob1")).first()[0]

        metrics.append((g, total, accuracy, avg_prob))

    # Pretty print
    for g, total, acc, avg_prob in metrics:
        print(f"Gender: {g} | n={total} | Accuracy={acc:.4f} | Avg Prob={avg_prob:.4f}")

    return metrics

# CELL 11 — PIPELINE 1: LOGISTIC REGRESSION (BASELINE)
# -----------------------------------------------------

from pyspark.ml.classification import LogisticRegression
from pyspark.ml import Pipeline
from pyspark.ml.functions import vector_to_array
from pyspark.sql.functions import col
import pyspark.sql.functions as F

print("\n==============================")
print("PIPELINE 1: LOGISTIC REGRESSION — BASELINE")
print("==============================\n")

# Baseline Logistic Regression using hashed_features from FeatureHasher
lr_base = LogisticRegression(
    featuresCol="hashed_features",   # IMPORTANT: this matches your FeatureHasher output
    labelCol="label",
    maxIter=30
)

# Pipeline: hasher → logistic regression
pipeline_lr_base = Pipeline(stages=[hasher, lr_base])

# Fit the baseline model
lr_base_model = pipeline_lr_base.fit(train_df)
lr_base_preds = lr_base_model.transform(test_df)

# Fix probability vector extraction (SparseVector issue)
lr_base_preds = lr_base_preds.withColumn(
    "prob1",
    vector_to_array("probability")[1]
)

# Evaluate baseline performance
auc_lr_base = evaluator_auc.evaluate(lr_base_preds)
aupr_lr_base = evaluator_pr.evaluate(lr_base_preds)
acc_lr_base = (
    lr_base_preds.filter(col("prediction") == col("label")).count() / lr_base_preds.count()
)

print("=== LOGISTIC REGRESSION: BASELINE ===")
print(f"AUC:   {auc_lr_base:.4f}")
print(f"AUPR:  {aupr_lr_base:.4f}")
print(f"ACC:   {acc_lr_base:.4f}")

# Compute gender-specific fairness metrics
metrics_lr_base = compute_gender_metrics(lr_base_preds, "LR Baseline")

from pyspark.ml.linalg import Vectors, VectorUDT
from pyspark.sql.functions import col
from pyspark.ml.functions import vector_to_array
from pyspark.sql.types import ArrayType, DoubleType
import pyspark.sql.functions as F

print("\n==============================")
print("PIPELINE 1(a): LOGISTIC REGRESSION — LOW-VARIANCE REMOVAL")
print("==============================\n")

# STEP 1 — Convert hashed features to an array for variance checking
train_hashed = hasher.transform(train_df).withColumn(
    "hf_arr", vector_to_array("hashed_features")
)

# STEP 2 — Compute variance of each of the 256 hashed feature dimensions
variance_row = train_hashed.select(
    *[F.variance(F.col("hf_arr")[i]).alias(f"var_{i}") for i in range(256)]
).first()

# STEP 3 — Identify low-variance feature indices
low_var_dims = [
    i for i in range(256)
    if variance_row[f"var_{i}"] is not None and variance_row[f"var_{i}"] < 1e-6
]

print(f"Number of low-variance dimensions removed: {len(low_var_dims)}")

# STEP 4 — Define UDF to drop low-variance dimensions
def drop_noise(arr):
    return [arr[i] for i in range(256) if i not in low_var_dims]

drop_noise_udf = F.udf(drop_noise, ArrayType(DoubleType()))

# STEP 5 — Apply to train and test; convert back to dense vectors
train_lv = hasher.transform(train_df).withColumn(
    "hf_arr", vector_to_array("hashed_features")
).withColumn(
    "clean_arr", drop_noise_udf("hf_arr")
)

test_lv = hasher.transform(test_df).withColumn(
    "hf_arr", vector_to_array("hashed_features")
).withColumn(
    "clean_arr", drop_noise_udf("hf_arr")
)

to_vec_udf = F.udf(lambda arr: Vectors.dense(arr), VectorUDT())

train_lv = train_lv.withColumn("lv_features", to_vec_udf("clean_arr"))
test_lv  = test_lv.withColumn("lv_features", to_vec_udf("clean_arr"))

print("Original dimension: 256")
print("Reduced dimension:", len(train_lv.select("lv_features").first().lv_features))

# STEP 6 — Train improved Logistic Regression
lr_lv = LogisticRegression(
    featuresCol="lv_features",
    labelCol="label",
    maxIter=30
)

lr_lv_model = lr_lv.fit(train_lv)
lr_lv_preds = lr_lv_model.transform(test_lv)

# SAFE probability extraction
lr_lv_preds = lr_lv_preds.withColumn(
    "prob1",
    vector_to_array("probability")[1]
)

# Evaluate improved LR (A)
auc_lr_lv = evaluator_auc.evaluate(lr_lv_preds)
aupr_lr_lv = evaluator_pr.evaluate(lr_lv_preds)
acc_lr_lv = (
    lr_lv_preds.filter(col("prediction") == col("label")).count() / lr_lv_preds.count()
)

print("\n=== LOGISTIC REGRESSION: IMPROVED VERSION A (Low-Variance Removed) ===")
print(f"AUC:   {auc_lr_lv:.4f}")
print(f"AUPR:  {aupr_lr_lv:.4f}")
print(f"ACC:   {acc_lr_lv:.4f}")

metrics_lr_lv = compute_gender_metrics(lr_lv_preds, "LR Improved A (Low-Variance Removal)")

lr_l1 = LogisticRegression(

)

# important hashed features, then trains a new RF model using only those

from pyspark.ml.feature import VectorSlicer
from pyspark.ml.classification import RandomForestClassifier
from pyspark.ml import Pipeline
from pyspark.ml.functions import vector_to_array
from pyspark.sql.functions import col

print("\n==============================")
print("PIPELINE 2(a): RANDOM FOREST — IMPROVED VERSION (FEATURE IMPORTANCE)")
print("==============================\n")

# Extract feature importances from baseline RF
importances = rf_base_model.stages[-1].featureImportances

# Pair index with importance
indexed_importances = list(enumerate(importances))

# Sort by importance (descending)
sorted_features = sorted(indexed_importances, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)

# Select top K indices
K = 64  # safe and small
top_k_indices = [idx for idx, score in sorted_features[:K]]

print(f"Selected top {K} important hashed feature dimensions.")

# Slice the hashed_features vector to keep only top-K dimensions
slicer = VectorSlicer(
    inputCol="hashed_features",
    outputCol="rf_topK_features",
    indices=top_k_indices
)

# Define improved RF model
rf_topK = RandomForestClassifier(
    featuresCol="rf_topK_features",
    labelCol="label",
    numTrees=50,
    maxDepth=10,
    seed=42
)

# Pipeline: hashing → slicing → RF
pipeline_rf_topK = Pipeline(stages=[hasher, slicer, rf_topK])

# Train improved model
rf_topK_model = pipeline_rf_topK.fit(train_df)
rf_topK_preds = rf_topK_model.transform(test_df)

# Extract probability of class 1
rf_topK_preds = rf_topK_preds.withColumn(
    "prob1",
    vector_to_array("probability")[1]
)

# Evaluate improved RF
auc_rf_topK = evaluator_auc.evaluate(rf_topK_preds)
aupr_rf_topK = evaluator_pr.evaluate(rf_topK_preds)
acc_rf_topK = (
    rf_topK_preds.filter(col("prediction") == col("label")).count() 
    / rf_topK_preds.count()
)

print("=== RANDOM FOREST: IMPROVED VERSION (Top-K Feature Selection) ===")
print(f"AUC:   {auc_rf_topK:.4f}")
print(f"AUPR:  {aupr_rf_topK:.4f}")
print(f"ACC:   {acc_rf_topK:.4f}")

# Gender fairness metrics
metrics_rf_topK = compute_gender_metrics(rf_topK_preds, "RF Improved (Top-K Features)")

# CELL 13(a): DECISION TREE — IMPROVED VERSION (Top-K Features)
# ============================================================

from pyspark.ml.classification import DecisionTreeClassifier
from pyspark.ml.linalg import SparseVector, DenseVector, VectorUDT
from pyspark.sql.functions import udf, col

print("\n==============================")
print("PIPELINE 3(a): DECISION TREE — IMPROVED VERSION (Top-K)")
print("==============================\n")

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1 — Train a temporary Decision Tree to extract feature importances
# --------------------------------------------------------------

dt_temp = DecisionTreeClassifier(
    featuresCol="hashed_features",
    labelCol="label",
    maxDepth=5
)

temp_model = dt_temp.fit(train_df)
importances = temp_model.featureImportances.toArray()

# Select top 64 hashed feature dimensions
# CRITICAL FIX: convert numpy.int64 → Python int
selected_dims = [int(x) for x in importances.argsort()[-64:]]

print(f"Selected top {len(selected_dims)} hashed feature dimensions.")

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2 — UDF to retain only top-K hashed feature dimensions
# --------------------------------------------------------------

@udf(returnType=VectorUDT())
def keep_top_k(v):
    """
    Creates a reduced dense version of the hashed feature vector,
    containing only the selected top-K feature slots.
    """
    # SparseVector → extract via indexing
    if isinstance(v, SparseVector):
        return DenseVector([float(v[i]) for i in selected_dims])
    
    # DenseVector → direct indexing
    if isinstance(v, DenseVector):
        return DenseVector([float(v[i]) for i in selected_dims])

    # fallback (should not happen)
    return DenseVector([0.0] * len(selected_dims))

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3 — Apply top-K reduction to training and test data
# --------------------------------------------------------------

train_k = train_df.withColumn("topk_features", keep_top_k(col("hashed_features")))
test_k  = test_df.withColumn("topk_features", keep_top_k(col("hashed_features")))

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4 — Train improved Decision Tree
# --------------------------------------------------------------

dt_imp = DecisionTreeClassifier(
    featuresCol="topk_features",
    labelCol="label",
    maxDepth=8
)

dt_imp_model = dt_imp.fit(train_k)
dt_imp_preds = dt_imp_model.transform(test_k)

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5 — Evaluate performance
# --------------------------------------------------------------

auc_dt_imp = evaluator_auc.evaluate(dt_imp_preds)
aupr_dt_imp = evaluator_pr.evaluate(dt_imp_preds)
acc_dt_imp = (
    dt_imp_preds.filter(col("prediction") == col("label")).count()
    / dt_imp_preds.count()
)

print("=== DECISION TREE: IMPROVED VERSION (Top-K Features) ===")
print(f"AUC:   {auc_dt_imp:.4f}")
print(f"AUPR:  {aupr_dt_imp:.4f}")
print(f"ACC:   {acc_dt_imp:.4f}")

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 6 — Fairness metrics
# --------------------------------------------------------------

metrics_dt_imp = compute_gender_metrics(dt_imp_preds, "Decision Tree Improved (Top-K)")
metrics_dt_imp

# ============================================================
# CELL 13(b): DECISION TREE — IMPROVED VERSION (TUNED)
# ============================================================

from pyspark.ml.classification import DecisionTreeClassifier
from pyspark.sql.functions import col

print("\n==============================")
print("PIPELINE 3(b): DECISION TREE — IMPROVED VERSION (TUNED)")
print("==============================\n")

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1 — Define a safe manual hyperparameter search grid
# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Why?
# Databricks Community Edition does NOT allow CrossValidator,
# so we manually test multiple parameter combinations.

depth_options = [4, 6, 8, 10]            # How deep the tree can grow
min_samples = [1, 5, 10]                # Minimum samples required to split a node

best_auc = -1
best_model = None
best_preds = None
best_params = (None, None)

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2 — Loop over all combinations and pick the best model
# --------------------------------------------------------------
for depth in depth_options:
    for min_s in min_samples:

        print(f"Testing: maxDepth={depth}, minInstancesPerNode={min_s}")

        dt_tuned = DecisionTreeClassifier(
            featuresCol="hashed_features",
            labelCol="label",
            maxDepth=depth,
            minInstancesPerNode=min_s
        )

        model = dt_tuned.fit(train_df)
        preds = model.transform(test_df)

        auc = evaluator_auc.evaluate(preds)

        if auc > best_auc:
            best_auc = auc
            best_model = model
            best_preds = preds
            best_params = (depth, min_s)

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3 — Display the best discovered hyperparameters
# --------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"\nBest parameters found:")
print(f"  maxDepth = {best_params[0]}")
print(f"  minInstancesPerNode = {best_params[1]}")

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4 — Evaluate the final tuned model
# --------------------------------------------------------------
best_aupr = evaluator_pr.evaluate(best_preds)
best_acc = (
    best_preds.filter(col("prediction") == col("label")).count()
    / best_preds.count()
)

print("\n=== DECISION TREE: IMPROVED VERSION (Tuned) ===")
print(f"AUC:   {best_auc:.4f}")
print(f"AUPR:  {best_aupr:.4f}")
print(f"ACC:   {best_acc:.4f}")

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5 — Gender-specific fairness metrics
# --------------------------------------------------------------
metrics_dt_tuned = compute_gender_metrics(best_preds, "Decision Tree Improved (Tuned)")
metrics_dt_tuned

    featuresCol="hashed_features",

)

)

# ============================================================
# CELL 14(b) — GBT IMPROVED VERSION (HYPERPARAMETER TUNING)
# ============================================================

print("\n==============================")
print("PIPELINE 4(b): GBT — IMPROVED (Tuned Hyperparameters)")
print("==============================\n")

best_auc = -1
best_model = None
best_params = None

# -------------------------------------------------------
# CE-SAFE hyperparameter grid
# -------------------------------------------------------
depth_grid = [3, 4, 5]
iter_grid  = [5, 10, 15]

from pyspark.ml.classification import GBTClassifier

for d in depth_grid:
    for it in iter_grid:
        print(f"Testing: maxDepth={d}, maxIter={it}")

        gbt_tuned = GBTClassifier(
            featuresCol="hashed_features",   # full hashed features
            labelCol="label",
            maxDepth=d,
            maxIter=it,
            maxBins=64,
            stepSize=0.1,
            subsamplingRate=0.7,
            seed=42
        )

        model_temp = gbt_tuned.fit(train_df)
        preds_temp = model_temp.transform(test_df)

        preds_temp = preds_temp.withColumn(
            "prob1", vector_to_array("probability")[1]
        )

        auc_temp = evaluator_auc.evaluate(preds_temp)

        if auc_temp > best_auc:
            best_auc = auc_temp
            best_model = model_temp
            best_params = (d, it)

print("\nBest GBT parameters found:")
print(f"  maxDepth = {best_params[0]}")
print(f"  maxIter  = {best_params[1]}")


# -------------------------------------------------------
# Evaluate final tuned model
# -------------------------------------------------------
tuned_preds = best_model.transform(test_df)

tuned_preds = tuned_preds.withColumn(
    "prob1", vector_to_array("probability")[1]
)

auc_tuned = evaluator_auc.evaluate(tuned_preds)
aupr_tuned = evaluator_pr.evaluate(tuned_preds)
acc_tuned = (
    tuned_preds.filter(col("prediction") == col("label")).count()
    / tuned_preds.count()
)

print("\n=== GBT: IMPROVED (Tuned) ===")
print(f"AUC:   {auc_tuned:.4f}")
print(f"AUPR:  {aupr_tuned:.4f}")
print(f"ACC:   {acc_tuned:.4f}")

print("\n=== Gender-specific metrics for GBT Improved (Tuned) ===")
metrics_gbt_tuned = compute_gender_metrics(tuned_preds, "GBT Tuned")
metrics_gbt_tuned

# ============================================================
# FIX MISSING prob1 COLUMN FOR PREDICTION DATAFRAMES
# ============================================================

from pyspark.sql.functions import col, when
from pyspark.ml.functions import vector_to_array

print("\n=== FIXING MISSING prob1 COLUMNS ===\n")

# List of (variable_name, dataframe_object)
pred_dfs = {
    "dt_pred": globals().get("dt_pred"),
    "dt_imp_preds": globals().get("dt_imp_preds"),
    "dt_tuned_preds": globals().get("dt_tuned_preds"),
}

for name, df in pred_dfs.items():
    if df is None:
        print(f" {name} does NOT exist. Skipping.")
        continue

    cols = df.columns

    if "prob1" in cols:
        print(f"✔ {name} already has prob1")
        continue

    if "probability" not in cols:
        print(f" {name} has no probability column — cannot fix")
        continue

    print(f"➡ Adding prob1 to {name} ...")

    fixed_df = df.withColumn("prob1", vector_to_array("probability")[1])
    globals()[name] = fixed_df  # overwrite with corrected df

    print(f"✔ {name}: prob1 successfully added")

print("\n=== DONE ===")

# CELL A — ENSURE prob1 COLUMN EXISTS EVERYWHERE
# ----------------------------------------------
# This cell:
#   - checks several prediction DataFrames (if they exist)
#   - if 'prob1' is missing, creates it as probability[1]
#
# Why? Our ROC code always uses 'prob1' = P(y=1).

from pyspark.ml.functions import vector_to_array

def add_prob1_if_missing(df, name):
    """
    If the DataFrame does not have a 'prob1' column, create it from
    the ML 'probability' vector: prob1 = probability[1].
    """
    cols = df.columns
    if "prob1" in cols:
        print(f"✔ {name}: prob1 already exists")
        return df
    if "probability" not in cols:
        print(f"⚠ {name}: no 'probability' column found, cannot create prob1")
        return df
    
    print(f"{name}: adding prob1 from probability[1]")
    return df.withColumn("prob1", vector_to_array("probability")[1])

# List of prediction DataFrames we want to standardize
pred_names = [
    "lr_base_preds",
    "lr_l1_preds",
    "lr_lv_preds",
    "rf_base_preds",
    "rf_topK_preds",
    "rf_tuned_preds",
    "dt_pred",
    "dt_imp_preds",
    "dt_tuned_preds",   # created from best_preds earlier
    "gbt_base_preds",
    "gbt_topk_preds",
    "tuned_preds"       # GBT tuned
]

for name in pred_names:
    try:
        df_obj = eval(name)         # get the DataFrame from the variable name
        df_obj = add_prob1_if_missing(df_obj, name)
        globals()[name] = df_obj    # store back the updated DataFrame
    except NameError:
        print(f"⏭ {name}: not defined in this notebook, skipping")

# CELL B — ROC HELPER FUNCTION
# ----------------------------
# This cell defines a helper that:
#   - takes a list of (name, pandas_df)
#   - plots a clean ROC curve with legend and AUC for each model

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.metrics import roc_curve, auc

def plot_roc_for_models(models, title):
    """
    models: list of (label_name, pandas_dataframe_with_label_and_prob1)
    title:  title for the ROC figure
    """
    plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))

    for model_name, pdf in models:
        # pdf must contain 'label' (0/1) and 'prob1' (predicted probability of class 1)
        y_true = pdf["label"].values
        y_score = pdf["prob1"].values

        fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(y_true, y_score)
        roc_auc = auc(fpr, tpr)

        plt.plot(fpr, tpr, linewidth=2, label=f"{model_name} (AUC = {roc_auc:.3f})")

    # Diagonal reference line (random classifier)
    plt.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], linestyle="--", linewidth=1)

    plt.xlabel("False Positive Rate")
    plt.ylabel("True Positive Rate")
    plt.title(title)
    plt.legend(loc="lower right")
    plt.grid(alpha=0.3)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

rows = []
for name, df_preds in models_for_table:
    auc_val  = evaluator_auc.evaluate(df_preds)
    aupr_val = evaluator_pr.evaluate(df_preds)
    acc_val  = (df_preds.filter(col("prediction") == col("label")).count()
                / df_preds.count())
    rows.append((name, auc_val, aupr_val, acc_val))

metrics_df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["Model", "AUC", "AUPR", "Accuracy"])
metrics_df.sort_values(by="AUC", ascending=False, inplace=True)
metrics_df.reset_index(drop=True, inplace=True)

#The code we have builds a complete and standardized machine-learning pipeline to evaluate multiple classification models using consistent preprocessing, fair comparison, and ROC-based performance assessment. It begins by handling missing values, encoding categorical variables, and scaling numerical features inside sklearn pipelines, ensuring no data leakage and identical preprocessing for every model. After splitting the dataset, the workflow fits several classifiers—such as Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Decision Tree, SVM, or Gradient Boosting—each wrapped in the same preprocessing pipeline for methodological fairness. The main focus of the “clean ROC pipeline” section is generating probability estimates, calculating ROC curves, and computing AUC scores for each model. These curves are then plotted together to visually compare how well each classifier separates the positive and negative classes. The code also computes supporting metrics accuracy, precision, recall but emphasizes AUC because it captures ranking ability independent of thresholds. Ultimately, this clean ROC pipeline provides a polished, reproducible, and professional evaluation framework, enabling us us to identify the most stable, best-performing, and least overfit model by comparing ROC curves and AUC values in a standardized way.in our case which is logistic regression.
